newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still mostly down late, cash up.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still mostly down late, cash up.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, hit by some profit taking after yesterday's rally, remained mostly lower late Wednesday in moderate trade, but forecasts for colder weather next week firmed the cash, sources said.
At 1430 EST, March was still down by 4.7 cents at $2.45 per million British thermal units, while April was 3.9 cents lower at $2.23. Most others were steady to down 1.8 cents.

"The forecast is helping the cash, but I don't know if the weather is going to be cold enough to support the (physical) market for long," said one East Coast trader, adding longs were bailing today after significant NYMEX gains yesterday.
Despite the colder weather ahead, traders said increasing pressure on storage operators and utilities to trim stocks, particularly in the East, was likely to limit any upside in the cash.

Technical traders said longs liquidated early today when a morning rally attempt stalled at resistance. They pegged March resistance in the low-$2.50s and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area. Trendline support was seen in the low-$2.30s and then at the November 5 low of $2.12.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report mostly were in the 155-170 bcf range compared to a 213 bcf decline in the same week last year.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed more than five cents Wednesday to the low-$2.60s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.50 area. New York city gate swing gas held relatively steady in the low-$3 level.
NYMEX said 21,122 Hub contracts traded by 1400 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1430 EST.
On the KCBT, March fell three cents to $2.17, while April was up a penny to $1.98. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.7 cents to 28 cents (NYMEX premium).
